cards.text: Jacob, also called Israel, calls all his sons together and tells them to gather around and listen to their father. He's about to tell them what will happen to them in the days to come. Friend, this is the kind of meeting where NOBODY is checking their phone.

cards.question: Jacob starts with his firstborn son, the oldest of them all. That's ___.

cards.text: Jacob calls Reuben his might and the beginning of his strength, excelling in honor, excelling in power. That's a review I'd FRAME and hang over my oven.

cards.question: After all that praise, Jacob says Reuben will keep on excelling.
Jacob tells Reuben he will no longer excel. What reason does Jacob give?

cards.text: Next, Jacob takes two sons at once, Simeon and Levi, and says their swords are weapons of violence. Friend, the only weapon I've got is this mustache, and the worst it ever did was knock over a cooling rack.

cards.question: Jacob says he hopes to join Simeon and Levi's council.
Jacob wants to stay out of Simeon and Levi's assembly. What reason does he give?

answers.text: They kill men in their anger
They refused to come to Egypt

cards.text: Then Jacob says, “Cursed be their anger, for it is strong, and their wrath, for it is cruel!” Look close, friend: it's the anger and the wrath he curses.

cards.question: Because of their anger, Jacob says he will ___ Simeon and Levi in Israel.

cards.text: Three sons in and Jacob is NOT holding back, so if I'm next, I'm sliding behind my mustache real slow. Then Jacob turns to Judah.

cards.question: Now it's Judah's turn. What does Jacob say Judah's brothers will do?

answers.text: Praise him and bow down to him
Turn on him and drive him out
Forget him and leave him behind

cards.text: Jacob says Judah is a young lion, coming back from the prey. Then he pictures him crouching and lying down, like a lioness.

cards.question: Jacob's lion picture makes Judah sound weak and easy to push around.

cards.text: Then Jacob says something will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet. It stays until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.

cards.question: Jacob says the ___ will not depart from Judah.

cards.text: Then Jacob says Judah ties his donkey to the vine and washes his garments in wine. Friend, my apron gets washed in plain old water, and this man is doing laundry in WINE.

cards.question: Jacob's picture of Judah keeps going: eyes darker than wine and teeth whiter than milk. What kind of life does it all show?

cards.text: Zebulun gets an OCEAN view: he'll live by the seashore and become a harbor for ships, with his border reaching to Sidon. Then Issachar, a strong donkey, lying down between the sheepfolds.

cards.question: Issachar sees that his resting place is good and his land is pleasant. What does he do?

answers.text: He bends his shoulder to the burden
He packs up and heads for Egypt
He fights his brothers for more land

cards.text: Dan will provide justice for his people as one of the tribes of Israel. Then Jacob says Dan will be a snake by the road, a viper in the path that bites the horse's heels.

cards.question: When Dan the snake bites the horse's heels, the horse's rider stays in the saddle.
Right in the middle of blessing his sons, Jacob stops and speaks one short line to someone else. Who does he speak to?
Jacob says Gad will be attacked by raiders and will never fight back.

cards.text: Asher's food will be rich, and he'll provide royal delicacies. Friend, I bake cookies for a LIVING, and I'm still a little jealous.
Naphtali is a doe set free that bears beautiful fawns. Then comes Joseph, a fruitful vine by a spring, whose branches scale the wall.
But it hasn't been easy for Joseph. The archers attacked him with bitterness and aimed at him in hostility.

cards.question: The archers aim at Joseph in hostility. What does Joseph do?

answers.text: He drops his bow and runs

cards.question: Jacob says Joseph's strong arms were tempered by someone's hands. Whose?

cards.text: The Almighty blesses Joseph with blessings of the heavens above and blessings of the depths below, and friend, that's not a sprinkle of blessing, that's the WHOLE JAR.

cards.question: Jacob wants his blessings to rest on Joseph's head. He calls Joseph the prince of his brothers.
Last comes Benjamin. Jacob calls him a ravenous wolf, so in the morning that wolf is ___ the prey.
When Jacob is done, he has given all twelve sons the exact same blessing.

cards.text: Then Jacob gives his sons one last instruction. He's about to be gathered to his people, and he tells them where to bury him.

cards.question: Jacob wants to be buried with his ___ in a cave in the land of ___.

cards.text: It's the cave in the field Abraham bought as a burial site, where Abraham and Sarah are buried, and Isaac and Rebekah. And Jacob buried one of his own wives there too.

cards.question: Which of his wives did Jacob bury in the cave with Abraham and Isaac?

cards.text: When Jacob finishes instructing his sons, he pulls his feet into the bed, breathes his last, and is gathered to his people. But stay close, friend, because this family's story isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: The question says Jacob will scatter Simeon and Levi "because of their anger." Genesis 49:7 curses their anger and then says "I will disperse them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel," but it never says the scattering is because of the anger. The card adds a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess Jacob's exact word (scatter, silence or humble). Nothing on the earlier cards lets a baker reason toward scattering over silencing or humbling, so the card tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can work out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card says Jacob pictures Judah "crouching and lying down, like a lioness." Genesis 49:9 says "Like a lion he crouches and lies down; like a lioness, who dares to rouse him?" The card moves the crouching from the lion comparison to the lioness comparison and drops "who dares to rouse him?"

The right answer, "He bends his shoulder to the burden," uses Bible phrasing. The wrong answers, "He packs up and heads for Egypt" and "He fights his brothers for more land," are casual and modern. The tone difference makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card asks only who Jacob speaks to in Genesis 49:18. No card tells what he says: "I await Your salvation, O LORD." The baker leaves Prep without the content of Jacob's only prayer in the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
